messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-2135 — hosted-inference/throughput-drop (p99 latency correlation + 15% drop in successful token throughput over 5m). Routing to Zoe (primary) and Nora (secondary). Auto-escalation in 3m if unacked. Link: https://pd/incidents/PD-2135
Zoe: acked. I'm checking ingress queues and the real-time dashboard. Noticing queue build on gpu-pool-hot.
Liam: paging in from home, will join in 2m. currently on kid-duty.
incidentbot: PagerDuty auto-escalation: alert escalated to Nora (secondary) — NO ACK.
incidentbot: PagerDuty auto-escalation: alert escalated to Tim (manager) — NO ACK.
Tim (manager): awake and here. what is customer impact?
Zoe: two medium tenants showing sustained backlog and job timeouts. No obvious 5xx spike, just tokens processed per second decreased. Inflight latency p99 jumped.
SRE-bot: recent events: a config change (rate-limiter throttle) deployed 6m ago to inference-proxy. Also node maintenance on gpu-pool-hot 4m ago (reboots).
Nora (secondary): just saw pages, ack'ing now, jumping on the call. apologies for delay — phone DND.
Liam: I can look at node health. pulling K8s logs and node metrics.
Zoe: hypothesis: combo of recent proxy throttle + node reboots reduced headroom and caused request pileups. If that's true, quick rollback of throttle could restore throughput.
Tim (manager): if rollback is low-risk, do it. Also consider auto-burst to dedicated-reserve pool to buy time.
Liam: checking proxy config diff. confirming throttle config lowered max-connections from 10k -> 6k at 2135002400. That seems likely culprit.
Zoe: rolling back throttle now to previous value. command: ```deployctl rollback inference-proxy --to=2026-03-12-10:12```. executing.
SRE-bot: rollback job accepted, will apply across regions sequentially.
Harper (support): I patched status page with "Investigating throughput degradation affecting some inference requests. We will update shortly."
Liam: also noticed some pods on gpu-pool-hot got stuck in CrashLoopBackOff after node reboots; restarting them should help. restarting problematic pods on infer-hot-2 and infer-hot-5. Command: ```kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/worker-infer --selector=pool=hot```
Nora (secondary): confirmed rollback of throttle propagated to EU region. Watching metrics.
incidentbot: PagerDuty note: alert acknowledged by Nora at 2135002542.
Zoe: after rollback and pod restarts, throughput climbing back: p99 latency dropping from 1.9s -> 0.7s, token TPS recovering.
Liam: manual node remediation completed on infer-hot-2 and infer-hot-5. kernel logs show previous eviction cascade due to transient oom-kill triggered by a memory leak in a sidecar injected last week. Noted.
Tim (manager): good catch. Let's keep dedicated-reserve burst available for 15m in case of reoccurrence. Zara in capacity team, please hold on to reserve capacity. (cc capacity team)
Harper (support): notified affected account managers with an interim note: "Throughput degradation caused delays; we've applied a rollback and restarted affected workers. Services are recovering. We'll follow up with RCA within 24 hours."
Zoe: mitigation summary in thread: rollback proxy throttle, restart stuck worker pods, node remediation. Immediate impact: customer throughput restored to normal within ~4 minutes. No customer data loss.
Nora (secondary): adding quick follow-ups: 1) remove that sidecar from future deploys until fixed; 2) add canary check for proxy max-connections change; 3) increase auto-scaling headroom temporarily for hot pool. I'm volunteering to own the canary check.
Liam: will file a bug for the sidecar memory leak with logs and OOM traces.
Tim (manager): assign owners: Nora -> canary check + hold on sidecar; Liam -> node remediation playbook update; Zoe -> incident timeline & RCA. Harper -> customer comms follow-through. I'll review RCA draft.
incidentbot: PagerDuty: PD-2135 status changed to Resolved by Zoe at 2135002666.
Zoe: closing bridge, leaving monitoring alerts on for 30m. thanks for quick responses. :thumbsup:
